chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who kills a woman deliberately, and the family of the woman intend to kill him: He (peace be upon him) said: That is for them, if they pay to his family half the blood-money (diyah). And if they accept the blood-money, then for them is half the blood-money of the man. And if the woman kills the man, she is killed due to it, and there is nothing for them except her soul.

And he (peace be upon him) said: The injuries of men and women are equal: the tooth of the woman is like the tooth of the man, and the bone of the woman is like the bone of the man, and the finger of the woman is like the finger of the man, until the injury reaches one-third of the blood-money. So when it reaches one-third of the blood-money, the blood-money of the man is doubled over the blood-money of the woman.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood-money or compensation paid for homicide or injury
key_terms.قِسَاص: Retaliation or equal retribution in kind

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood-money and retaliation between men and women in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between Qisas (retaliation) and Diyah (blood-money) in homicide, emphasizing that while retaliation for a woman's life is strictly limited to her own life, financial compensation varies by gender. It further establishes a proportional scaling for injuries, where male and female injuries are treated equally up to one-third of the full Diyah, after which the male's compensation doubles, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the valuation of bodily integrity.
